body.translated_text: <s>Pañcakrama</s> (The Five Stages)

[1]
<s>Vajrajāpakrama</s> (The Stage of Vajra Recitation) — the First
Oṃ, homage to the <s>Buddha</s>.

children.translated_text: Having bowed to the Lord, the embodiment of all <s>Buddhas</s>, the glorious <s>Mahāsukha</s> (Great Bliss),
I shall expound the <s>Vajrajāpakrama</s> (Stage of Vajra Recitation) in accordance with the <s>Yogatantra</s>. (Pk 1.1)
For those established in the <s>utpattikrama</s> (generation stage) who aspire to the <s>niṣpannakrama</s> (completion stage),
this method has been fashioned by the fully awakened <s>Buddhas</s> like a staircase. (Pk 1.2)
The life-force of beings, called <s>vāyu</s> (wind), is the doer of all actions;
it is the vehicle of <s>vijñāna</s> (consciousness), fivefold in nature, and tenfold again. (Pk 1.3)
Through the sequential [practice of] <s>vāyutattva</s> (wind principle), one should enter into <s>mantratattva</s> (mantra principle);
having arrived at the realization of <s>mantra</s>, <s>vajrajāpa</s> (vajra recitation) is well learned. (Pk 1.4)
The <s>mantrī</s> (practitioner) established in <s>vajrajāpa</s> attains the realization of <s>citta</s> (mind);
abiding in <s>māyopama-samādhi</s> (illusion-like concentration), one enters the <s>bhūtakoṭi</s> (limit of reality). (Pk 1.5)
Rising from the <s>bhūtakoṭi</s>, one attains <s>advayajñāna</s> (non-dual knowledge);
established in <s>yuganaddha-samādhi</s> (unified pair concentration), one no longer perceives anything whatsoever. (Pk 1.6)
This is called <s>niṣpannayoga</s> (completed yoga), and he becomes the great <s>Vajradhara</s>;
endowed with the excellence of all forms, he is born as the <s>Sarvajña</s> (Omniscient One). (Pk 1.7)
The future, the past, and the present — the three modes of existence —
in an instant he sees them all completely, through the purity of <s>prabhāsvara</s> (clear light). (Pk 1.8)
This <s>tattva</s> (principle) is established in the <s>tantra</s>, well sealed in the <s>Śrīsamāja</s> (Guhyasamāja);
it should be understood from the mouth of the <s>guru</s>, in accordance with the explanatory <s>tantras</s>. (Pk 1.9)

body.translated_text: Here, first of all, the introductory passage on <s>vāyutattva</s> (wind principle) is extracted from the root <s>sūtra</s>:

children.translated_text: One should contemplate a mustard seed at the tip of the nose; in that mustard seed, the entire animate and inanimate [universe];
one should meditate on the delightful station of <s>jñāna</s> (knowledge), the secret fashioned by knowledge. (Pk 1.10)
The great jewel of five colors, the mere size of a mustard seed,

children.text: nāsikāgre prayatnena bhāvayed yogataḥ sadā || Pk_1.11 ||
children.translated_text: should always be meditated upon with effort at the tip of the nose, through <s>yoga</s>. (Pk 1.11)

body.translated_text: Thus, in <s>sandhābhāṣā</s> (intentional language), the explanation of this <s>vajrapada</s> (vajra stage) is stated in the <s>Caturdevīvyākhyātantra</s>:

children.text: tad devi sampravakṣyāmi sārāt sārataraṃ param |
children.translated_text: O <s>Devī</s>, I shall proclaim that which is the supreme essence of essences,

children.text: rahasyaṃ sarvabuddhānāṃ yat tat sarvātmani sthitam || Pk_1.12 ||
children.translated_text: the secret of all <s>Buddhas</s>, which abides in the Self of all. (Pk 1.12)

body.text:
paścajñānamayaṃ tattvaṃ sarṣapasthūlamātrakam |
tasya madhye sthito devo hyavyakto vyaktarūpavān || iti | Pk_1.13 ||
body.translated_text:
The <s>tattva</s> (principle) consisting of the five <s>jñānas</s> (knowledges), the mere size of a mustard seed —
in its center dwells the deity, unmanifest yet having manifest form. (Pk 1.13)
In the <s>Samājottara</s> also, illuminating this meaning, it says:

children.translated_text: The breath consisting of the five <s>jñānas</s>, having the nature of the five elements,
having exhaled it at the tip of the lotus-nose, one should visualize it in the form of a ball. (Pk 1.14)

children.text: svamantraṃ hṛdaye dhyātvā cittaṃ bindugataṃ nyaset || Pk_1.15 |
children.translated_text: having meditated on one's own <s>mantra</s> in the heart, one should place the <s>citta</s> (mind) at the <s>bindu</s> (point). (Pk 1.15)

body.translated_text: The great jewel of five colors is known as <s>prāṇāyāma</s> (breath control);
The detailed explanation of this is also stated in the explanatory <s>tantra</s> called <s>Vajramālā</s>:

children.translated_text: The mustard seed at the tip of the nose is the visualization of <s>prāṇāyāma</s>;
the five rays established in <s>prāṇāyāma</s> arise from the nature of a <s>Buddha</s>. (Pk 1.16)
Going upward from the nose, issuing forth as left and right pairs,

children.text: stabdhaśceti caturdhāsmād velā ādhyātmikā smṛtā || Pk_1.17 ||
children.translated_text: and standing still — thus fourfold; these are known as the inner time-periods (<s>ādhyātmikā velā</s>). (Pk 1.17)
At the throat, heart, navel, and secret lotus, one should indicate the movements of going and coming;

children.text: vihared ardhayāmikāṃ velāṃ paripāṭyā yathākramam || Pk_1.18 ||
children.translated_text: one should practice the half-watch time-period in proper sequence and order. (Pk 1.18)
The ray issuing from the right is the <s>hutabhuk-maṇḍala</s> (fire circle);
it is clearly red in color, and <s>Padmanātha</s> (Lord of the Lotus) is the deity here. (Pk 1.19)
The ray issuing from the left is designated as the <s>vāyu-maṇḍala</s> (wind circle);
it appears green-dark, and <s>Karmanātha</s> (Lord of Action) is the deity here. (Pk 1.20)
The ray issuing from both is yellow in color, of great radiance;
this is the <s>Māhendra-maṇḍala</s> (circle of great Indra), and <s>Ratnanātha</s> (Lord of Jewels) is the deity here. (Pk 1.21)
Standing still, of slow movement, white like jasmine and the moon,

children.text: maṇḍalaṃ vāruṇaṃ caitad vajranātho 'tra devatā || Pk_1.22 ||
children.translated_text: this is the <s>Vāruṇa-maṇḍala</s> (water circle), and <s>Vajranātha</s> (Lord of the Vajra) is the deity here. (Pk 1.22)
The <s>vāyu</s> (wind) pervades the entire body and sets all activities in motion;
it is of the nature of <s>Vairocana</s> and departs from the body at death. (Pk 1.23)
This <s>vāyutattva</s> (wind principle) is clearly of the nature of the five <s>jñānas</s> (knowledges);

children.text: tārkikā na prajānanti agamyaṃ bālayoginām || Pk_1.24 ||
children.translated_text: logicians do not comprehend it — it is inaccessible to novice <s>yogīs</s>. (Pk 1.24)

body.translated_text: Having thus expounded the <s>vāyutattva</s> (wind principle), now the introductory passage on <s>mantratattva</s> (mantra principle) is extracted from the root <s>sūtra</s>:

body.text: sarvatathāgatakāyavākcittarahasyaṃ sarvatantrahṛdayasañcodanaṃ nāma paramaguhyaṃ svakāyavākcittavajrebhyo vākpathaniruktyā mantrasamuccayamudājahāra oṃ āḥ hūṃ |
body.translated_text: The secret of the body, speech, and mind of all <s>Tathāgatas</s>, the supreme secret called 'the urging of the heart of all <s>tantras</s>' — from his own body, speech, and mind <s>vajras</s>, he uttered the collection of <s>mantras</s> by the path of speech: Oṃ Āḥ Hūṃ.

children.translated_text: Through recitation that follows the meaning, which is without inherent nature and beautiful,

children.text: vicāraṇā tryadhvabuddhebhyo vajrajāpaḥ sa ucyate || Pk_1.25 ||
children.translated_text: the investigation [arising] from the <s>Buddhas</s> of the three times — that is called <s>vajrajāpa</s> (vajra recitation). (Pk 1.25)

children.text: bhikṣāśinā na japtavyaṃ na ca bhaikṣarato bhavet |
children.translated_text: One who eats alms should not recite [externally], nor should one be attached to begging;
one should recite the <s>mantra</s> with undivided limbs, which accomplishes the enjoyment of all desires. (Pk 1.26)

body.translated_text: This is the introductory passage; its detailed explanation is stated in the <s>Sandhyāvyākaraṇavyākhyātantra</s>; it is extracted here:

children.translated_text: Then the glorious one replied to the mighty <s>Mahāvairocana</s>, the all-pervading Lord:
"This mind is of universal form, arising from the birth of all beings. (Pk 1.27)

children.text: jātaṃ san niḥsvabhāvo 'pi bhāvākhyaṃ tu pratītyataḥ |
children.translated_text: Though born, it is without inherent nature; yet through dependent origination it is called 'existence';

children.text: kṛtvā cānubhavaṃ samyag bodhicittaṃ khatulyakam || Pk_1.28 ||
children.translated_text: having rightly experienced it, [one realizes] <s>bodhicitta</s> (awakening mind) is equal to space. (Pk 1.28)
To accomplish the welfare of the world, one should teach it to the highest beings;
knowing merely the means of practice, as elaborated in the <s>tantra</s>. (Pk 1.29)

body.text:
ācāryā vayamityevaṃ vadantyāgāmikā vibho |
yad vākyaṃ mametyevamuktvā kṣipanti bāliśāḥ |
sandhyāya bodhicittaṃ te na vidanti yathārthataḥ || iti | Pk_1.30 ||

children.translated_text: Just as the <s>Bhagavān</s>, the master, the mighty all-pervading <s>Mahāvairocana</s>,
three times uttered the word 'excellent' and spoke this to <s>Vajrapāṇi</s>: (Pk 1.31)
"I shall explain by way of classification, from the standpoint of the <s>tattva</s> (truth) that is free from conceptual elaboration:
utterance, apprehension, the symbolic, and the ultimate. (Pk 1.32)
Utterance is the ordinary, the apprehension of <s>Buddha</s>-form;
the symbolic is called <s>mantratattva</s> (mantra principle); <s>tathatā</s> (suchness) is the ultimate. (Pk 1.33)
Beginning with one, in the midst of nine, one who is not bound by the ten —

children.text: tamabaddhaṃ vijānīyāt sa vetti parasampadam || Pk_1.34 ||
children.translated_text: know that one as the unbound; he knows the supreme attainment. (Pk 1.34)
Vowels, consonants, and syllables follow the count of nine;

children.text: ' abaddhānyonyasaṃyoogād yo vetti sa jagadguruḥ || Pk_1.35 ||
children.translated_text: one who knows them as unbound through mutual combination is the <s>Jagadguru</s> (World Teacher). (Pk 1.35)
Conjoined with the final element, established in the sixteenth <s>kalā</s> (digit),
joined with five groups of five, arranged in sets of four and three, (Pk 1.36)
with <s>anusvāra</s>, with length, without <s>guṇa</s>-sandhi,

children.text: hrasvaṃ samastavākyaṃ syānna cānekaṃ na caikakam || Pk_1.37 ||
children.translated_text: the short [form] would be the complete utterance — neither many nor one. (Pk 1.37)

children.text: ye varṇāḥ pṛṣṭhataḥ proktā abhimukhāśca ye punaḥ |
children.translated_text: Those syllables spoken from behind and those facing forward,
feminine, masculine, and neuter — they are conceived from verbal roots and so forth. (Pk 1.38)
Knowing [them as] conjoined below and above, one should apply [them] with wisdom;
this utterance-<s>mantra</s> is born of the nature of non-inherent-nature. (Pk 1.39)
Then the matured form that perceives the deity —
the symbolic, abiding in the three <s>tattvas</s>, has the characteristic of natural recitation. (Pk 1.40)
The knowledge indicated by the syllable 'A' becomes the heart of the <s>Buddha</s>;
the syllable 'Oṃ' emanates beings, conceived as foremost in <s>Buddha</s>-form. (Pk 1.41)
The syllable 'Hūṃ' withdraws beings; the syllable 'Āḥ' stabilizes them;

children.text: praveśaśva sthitiścaiva vyutthānaṃ ca krameṇa ca || Pk_1.42 ||
children.translated_text: entry, abiding, and arising — in sequence. (Pk 1.42)
One should recite the <s>mantra</s> with undivided limbs, established in the station of <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom) and <s>upāya</s> (means);
the recitation beginning with <s>Pāṇḍarā</s> is proclaimed as two hundred and twenty-five. (Pk 1.43)
Multiplied by four correctly, four hundred [and]
nine hundred as is known, with twenty-four cycles;

children.text: pratyutpādād bhavet tatra dvyayutaṃ śataṣoḍaśam || Pk_1.44 ||
children.translated_text: from the product there arises twenty thousand one hundred and sixty. (Pk 1.44)

body.translated_text: This very [practice] during the inner time-period is illuminated in the <s>Samājottara</s>:

children.translated_text: By the method of <s>vidyā</s>-conduct, through the practice of the four <s>sandhyās</s> (junctures),
one should recite the <s>mantra</s> with undivided limbs, one hundred thousand by the count of syllables. (Pk 1.45)
The <s>yogī</s> should abandon external recitation, which is an obstacle to meditation;

children.text: mantrārtho bhagavān vajrī vajrātmātra kathaṃ japet || Pk_1.46 ||
children.translated_text: the meaning of the <s>mantra</s> is the <s>Bhagavān</s>, the <s>Vajrī</s> himself — here being the <s>vajra</s>-self, how would one recite? (Pk 1.46)
One obtains an elephant immediately; one should search for the elephant's footprint;

children.text: mantramūrtiḥ svayaṃ sākṣāt kimanyattu gaveṣate || Pk_1.47 ||
children.translated_text: the <s>mantra</s>-embodiment itself is directly present — what else would one seek? (Pk 1.47)

children.text: api ca vajradhṛk kaścit trisaṃyogānvito naraḥ |
children.translated_text: Furthermore, a certain <s>vajra</s>-holder, a person endowed with the triple union,

children.text: āvāhanavisarjanaṃ syāt tathā sthāpanameva ca || Pk_1.48 ||
children.translated_text: there would be invocation, dismissal, and also establishment. (Pk 1.48)
Invocation is by entry, dismissal by haste,

children.text: vāṣpeṇa sthāpanaṃ tat syād viśvastāt siddhiruttamā || Pk_1.49 ||
children.translated_text: establishment would be by vapor; from trust comes the supreme <s>siddhi</s> (accomplishment). (Pk 1.49)
In haste, in binding, and in vapor — the application of <s>mantra</s> has been taught.
at the root of the ear of the disciple, by the <s>ācārya</s> (master), with great effort. || Pk_1.50 ||
Now, for the lords of <s>yoga</s>, the divine method is shown;
I shall teach the secret syllable, which grants the fruit of <s>yoga-siddhi</s> (yogic attainment). || Pk_1.51 ||
By merely thinking of which, <s>yogins</s> become bestowers of boons;
by employing the first syllable, one always performs exhalation. || Pk_1.52 ||
Combined with the eighth ending, the letter U with <s>bindu</s> (dot);
the <s>yogin</s> performs inhalation — this is said to be obtained from delight. || Pk_1.53 ||

children.text: ayutadvayaṃ sahasraṃ ca ṣaṭ śatāni tathaiva ca |
children.translated_text: Twenty thousand and one thousand, and six hundred as well;

children.text: ahorātreṇa yogīndro japasaṃkhyāṃ karoti ca || Pk_1.54 ||
children.translated_text: in one day and night, the lord of <s>yogins</s> performs this count of <s>japa</s> (recitation). || Pk_1.54 ||
Thus in the secret twilight, the subtle <s>yoga</s> is revealed;

children.text: dhyānādhyayanavītaṃ tu tathāpi jāpa ucyate || Pk_1.55 ||
children.translated_text: free from meditation and study, yet it is called <s>jāpa</s> (recitation). || Pk_1.55 ||
By this <s>vajrajāpa</s> (diamond recitation), having performed the practice according to the prescribed method,
one should accomplish all tasks through the <s>māyopamasamādhi</s> (illusion-like concentration). || Pk_1.56 ||

body.translated_text: Here it is stated in the <s>Advayasamatā-mahāyoga-tantra</s>:

children.translated_text: "Having recited the incomparable <s>mantra</s>, the practitioner devoted to <s>sādhana</s> should accomplish [the goal];

children.text: sidhyate tasya trailokyaṃ māsaikena na saṃśayaḥ || Pk_1.57 ||
children.translated_text: the three worlds are perfected for him within a single month — there is no doubt." || Pk_1.57 ||

children.text: ṣaḍ lakṣāṇi japitvā tu mantraṃ jñānasamudbhavam |
children.translated_text: "Having recited six hundred thousand times the <s>mantra</s> born of <s>jñāna</s> (wisdom),

children.text: vajrasattvaṃ namaskṛtya pūrṇamāsyāṃ sa sidhyati || Pk_1.58 ||
children.translated_text: having bowed to <s>Vajrasattva</s>, on the full moon day, one attains <s>siddhi</s> (perfection)." || Pk_1.58 ||

children.text: na tasya vratamākhyātaṃ nākṣasūtraṃ na mantrakam |
children.translated_text: For him, no vow is prescribed, no rosary, no <s>mantra</s> [recitation],

children.text: dhāraṇā homakarmāṇi varjyante ca parāparam || Pk_1.59 ||
children.translated_text: <s>dhāraṇā</s> (concentration) and fire-offering rituals are dispensed with, both the higher and lower. || Pk_1.59 ||
By the meaning of the letter YA, whatever one desiring <s>siddhi</s> [seeks],
by the threefold beginning with the letter RA, that task proceeds. || Pk_1.60 ||
In the <s>maṇḍalas</s> (circles) of <s>Agni</s> (fire), <s>Vāyu</s> (wind), <s>Mahendra</s> (great Indra), and <s>Varuṇa</s> (water),

children.text: ardhayāmikavelāyāṃ dvau dvau karmaṇi tiṣṭhataḥ || Pk_1.61 ||
children.translated_text: at the time of half a <s>yāma</s> (watch), two actions each are established. || Pk_1.61 ||
One devoted to worship becomes worthy of worship; one devoted to <s>jāpa</s> (recitation) is purified;

children.text: agnihotraparo bhūtiṃ mokṣaṃ dhyānaparo labhet || Pk_1.62 ||
children.translated_text: one devoted to <s>agnihotra</s> (fire-offering) [gains] prosperity; one devoted to meditation obtains <s>mokṣa</s> (liberation). || Pk_1.62 ||
Having known this thus, the <s>mantrin</s> (adept) should act like a child in the world;
then the <s>mantras</s> are perfected, through non-conceptual singular <s>dharmatā</s> (nature of reality). || Pk_1.63 ||

body.text:
mantratattvamidaṃ vyaktaṃ vāgvajrasya prasādhanam |
jñānatrayaprabhedena cittamātre niyojayed || iti || Pk_1. 64 ||
body.translated_text: This <s>mantra-tattva</s> (mantra-reality) is manifest, the accomplishment of <s>vāgvajra</s> (speech-vajra); / through the division of the three <s>jñānas</s> (wisdoms), one should apply [oneself] to mind-only. || Thus || Pk_1.64 ||

children.translated_text: One who scorns the <s>guru</s>, a wicked person, displeased, arrogant with <s>mantras</s>, proud of book-learning,

children.text: aśraddadhānastvabhiṣekahīno vārtā kramasyāpi ca tasya noktā || Pk_1.65 ||
children.translated_text: faithless and lacking <s>abhiṣeka</s> (consecration) — even the mention of the <s>krama</s> (stages) is not told to such a one. || Pk_1.65 ||

children.text: yaḥ śraddadhāno gurubhaktiraktaḥ śuśrūṣaṇāyāṃ ca sadābhiyuktaḥ |
children.translated_text: One who is faithful, devoted to the <s>guru</s> with devotion, always engaged in service,

children.text: grāhyaḥ śrutiṃ naiva dhanaṃ nirīkṣyaṃ gurupradhāno 'ya guruprasādaḥ || Pk_1.66 ||
children.translated_text: should be accepted; wealth should not be considered — this is the <s>guru</s>'s principal gift, the <s>guru</s>'s grace. || Pk_1.66 ||

children.text: girīndramūrdhnaḥ prapatet tu kaścit neccheccyutiṃ tu cyavate tathāpi |
children.translated_text: One might fall from the peak of the lord of mountains, not wishing to fall, yet one falls nonetheless;

children.text: guruprasādāptahitopadeśa icchenna moktaṃ sa tathāpi muktaṃḥ || Pk_1.67 ||
children.translated_text: one who has received beneficial instruction through the <s>guru</s>'s grace, even not wishing liberation, is nevertheless liberated. || Pk_1.67 ||

body.translated_text: || The <s>Vajrajāpa-krama</s> (Stage of Diamond Recitation) is completed. ||

children.translated_text: This is the composition of the venerable <s>Nāgārjunapāda</s>.
The extent of this text is seventy-six [verses].

body.translated_text: The first <s>krama</s> (stage). ||
[2] The <s>Sarvaśuddhi-viśuddhi-krama</s>, otherwise named <s>Anuttara-sandhi</s>, the second [stage]:
Homage to the glorious <s>Vajrasattva</s>.

children.translated_text: Salutation to you, salutation to you, salutation to you — homage, homage!

children.text: evaṃ stute namaste 'stu kaḥ stotā kaśca saṃstutaḥ || Pk_2.1 ||
children.translated_text: When thus praised, 'salutation to you!' — who is the praiser and who is praised? || Pk_2.1 ||

children.text: yathā jalaṃ jale nyastaṃ ghṛtaṃ caiva yathā ghṛte |
children.translated_text: Just as water placed in water, just as <s>ghṛta</s> (clarified butter) in <s>ghṛta</s>,

children.text: svakīyaṃ ca svayaṃ paśyej jñānaṃ yatreha vandanā || Pk_2.2 ||
children.translated_text: one should see one's own [nature] by oneself — where there is <s>jñāna</s> (wisdom), there is worship. || Pk_2.2 ||
However, without the paths of the omniscient, that is not attained;
covered by a veil of darkness, through grace one may reach the island [of liberation]. || Pk_2.3 ||

children.text: śūnyaṃ ca atiśūnyaṃ ca mahāśunyaṃ tṛtīyakam |
children.translated_text: <s>Śūnya</s> (emptiness) and <s>atiśūnya</s> (extreme emptiness), <s>mahāśūnya</s> (great emptiness) as the third,
and <s>sarvaśūnya</s> (universal emptiness) as the fourth — distinguished by cause and effect. || Pk_2.4 ||
From the union of <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom) and <s>upāya</s> (means), the accomplished is perceived;
and from the perceived and accomplished, <s>sarvaśūnya</s> (universal emptiness) is luminous. || Pk_2.5 ||
The purification of the causal stages, through the yoga of the three <s>vijñānas</s> (consciousnesses);
from the union of the three emptinesses, the unsurpassed state is attained. || Pk_2.6 ||

children.text: ālokaśśūnyaṃ prajñā ca cittaṃ ca paratantrakam |
children.translated_text: <s>Āloka</s> (light) is emptiness and <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom), and <s>citta</s> (mind) is dependent [in nature];
I shall now clearly teach the expansion of <s>prakṛti</s> (innate nature). || Pk_2.7 ||
<s>Virāga</s> (dispassion), the middling, and the intense likewise;
the coming and going of mind, and sorrow and such as the third. || Pk_2.8 ||
The gentle, trembling, and fearful, the moderately fearful and extremely fearful;
<s>tṛṣṇā</s> (craving), moderate craving, and extreme craving, and <s>upādāna</s> (grasping) likewise. || Pk_2.9 ||
The inauspicious, hunger and thirst, <s>vedanā</s> (feeling) and equal feeling,
extreme feeling, and the moment, the state of knower, struck, and the ground of retention. || Pk_2.10 ||
Reflection and shame, compassion and three [degrees of] affection,

children.text: cakitaṃ saṃśayaścaiva mātsaryaṃ ceti kīrtitāḥ || Pk_2.11 ||
children.translated_text: agitation, doubt, and jealousy — thus they are declared. || Pk_2.11 ||
Thirty-three <s>prakṛtis</s> (natures), self-experienced by embodied beings,
shown in the form of conventional clarity, they are designated as 'night.' || Pk_2.12 ||

children.text: strīsaṃjñā tathā proktā mandākārā tathaiva ca |
children.translated_text: They are also called 'woman,' of gentle appearance,
and also called 'left' — the moon-<s>maṇḍala</s> lotus. || Pk_2.13 ||
For the purpose of stabilization, the first vowel with <s>bindu</s> (dot);
resembling the rays of the moon, born of <s>āloka-jñāna</s> (light-wisdom). || Pk_2.14 ||
<s>Ālokābhāsa</s> (appearance of light) is said to be excellent, <s>atiśūnya</s> (extreme emptiness) is the means;

children.text: parikalpitaṃ tathā proktaṃ proktaṃ caitasikaṃ tathā || Pk_2.15 ||
children.translated_text: it is also called 'imagined,' and also 'mental.' || Pk_2.15 ||
<s>Rāga</s> (passion), the passionate, satisfaction, moderate satisfaction, and extreme satisfaction;

children.text: harṣaṇaṃ caiva prāmodyaṃ vismayo hasitaṃ tathā || Pk_2.16 ||
children.translated_text: joy and delight, wonder and laughter likewise. || Pk_2.16 ||
Gladness and embracing, and likewise kissing and sucking;

children.text: dhairyaṃ vīryaṃ ca mānaśca kartṛhartṛbalāni ca || Pk_2.17 ||
children.translated_text: firmness, vigor, and pride, and the powers of the doer, the seizer, and strength. || Pk_2.17 ||
Enthusiasm and daring, and likewise supreme daring,

children.text: madhyamaṃ sāhasaṃ rādraṃ vilāso vairameva ca || Pk_2.18 ||
children.translated_text: moderate daring, the fierce, play, and enmity. || Pk_2.18 ||

children.text: śubhaṃ ca vāk sphuṭā satyamasatyaṃ niścayastathā |
children.translated_text: The auspicious, clear speech, truth and untruth, and certainty likewise;
the quality of being a giver without grasping, urging, and heroism likewise;

children.text: alajjā dhūrtaduṣṭaśca haṭhaḥ kuṭila eva ca |
children.translated_text: shamelessness, the deceitful and wicked, obstinacy, and crookedness;
forty <s>prakṛtis</s> (natures), momentary, born from <s>atiśūnya</s> (extreme emptiness). || Pk_2.20 ||
They are designated as 'day,' 'man,' of harsh form, and 'right';

children.text: sūryamaṇḍalasaṃjñā ca vajrasaṃjñā tathaiva ca || Pk_2.21 ||
children.translated_text: also designated as 'sun-<s>maṇḍala</s>' and '<s>vajra</s>.' || Pk_2.21 ||
That same phase should be known, adorned with the two <s>bindus</s> (dots);
resembling the rays of the sun, born from the union of <s>ālokābhāsa</s> (appearance of light). || Pk_2.22 ||
The perception of <s>āloka</s> (light) and <s>upalabdha</s> (the perceived) likewise;

children.text: pariniṣpannakaṃ caiva avidyā caiva nāmataḥ || Pk_2.23 ||
children.translated_text: also the fully accomplished, and named <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance). || Pk_2.23 ||
These synonyms of the state of <s>mahāśūnya</s> (great emptiness) have been taught by the <s>Jinas</s> (Victorious Ones);
the moment of middle passion, forgetfulness, and delusion. || Pk_2.24 ||
Silence, weariness, laziness, and sluggishness likewise;

children.text: avidyāyāḥ kṣaṇāḥ sapta vijñeyāḥ sukṣmayogibhiḥ || Pk_2.25 ||
children.translated_text: seven moments of <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) should be known by subtle <s>yogins</s>. || Pk_2.25 ||
When the seed is not joined with the <s>bindu</s> (drop), when the <s>vāyu</s> (wind) has not gone out through the door,
when the light is perceived — that is the characteristic of the fully accomplished. || Pk_2.26 ||

children.text: etāḥ prakṛtayaḥ sūkṣmāḥ śataṃ ṣaṣṭyuttaraṃ divā |
children.translated_text: These subtle <s>prakṛtis</s> (natures), one hundred and sixty, by day
and by night also operate, caused by the vehicle of <s>vāyu</s> (wind). || Pk_2.27 ||

children.text: kṣaṇe lave muhūrtte ca nimeṣe mātrake tathā |
children.translated_text: In a <s>kṣaṇa</s> (moment), a <s>lava</s>, a <s>muhūrta</s>, a <s>nimeṣa</s> (blink), and a <s>mātrā</s> (measure) likewise;
a <s>kṣaṇa</s> is the state of a flash, a <s>lava</s> is the rolling of a mustard seed. || Pk_2.28 ||
A breath is a <s>muhūrta</s>, a <s>nimeṣa</s> is the blinking of an eye;

children.text: mātrā tu hastatālaṃ syāt kṣaṇādīnāṃ tu lakṣaṇam || Pk_2.29 ||
children.translated_text: a <s>mātrā</s> is a clap of the hand — such are the characteristics of <s>kṣaṇa</s> and the rest. || Pk_2.29 ||
<s>Jñāna</s> (wisdom) is mere awareness, with a characteristic like space;
but there is a distinction in it, through the nature of twilight, night, and day. || Pk_2.30 ||
<s>Āloka</s> (light), <s>ālokābhāsa</s> (appearance of light), and <s>ālokopalabdhi</s> (perception of light);
mind is said to be threefold — its basis is now described. || Pk_2.31 ||
<s>Jñāna</s> (wisdom), mixed with <s>vāyu</s> (wind) in subtle form,
issuing forth through the sense-channels, grasps sense-objects. || Pk_2.32 ||
When the <s>vāyu</s> (wind), endowed with appearance, has become the vehicle,

children.text: tadā tatprakṛtīḥ sarvā astavyastāḥ pravartayet || Pk_2.33 ||
children.translated_text: then it sets in motion all those <s>prakṛtis</s> (natures) in a scattered manner. || Pk_2.33 ||

children.text: yatra yatra sthito vāyustāṃ tāṃ prakṛtimudvahet |
children.translated_text: Wherever the <s>vāyu</s> (wind) abides, it carries forth that particular <s>prakṛti</s> (nature);

children.text: yāvat samīraṇotpādo nābhāso niścalo bhavet || Pk_2.34 ||
children.translated_text: as long as wind arises, the appearance will not be still. || Pk_2.34 ||
The cause of the two appearances would be the conceptualization of self-nature;
it would be of both aspects, what is the perception of light. || Pk_2.35 ||
Of all illusions, the illusion of woman is the most excellent;
this distinction of the three <s>jñānas</s> (wisdoms) is clearly perceived right here. || Pk_2.36 ||
<s>Rāga</s> (passion) and <s>virāga</s> (dispassion) and the interval between the two — thus three;
through the union of the two faculties, from the meeting of <s>vajra</s> and <s>padma</s> (lotus). || Pk_2.37 ||
The union of the two knowledges (<s>jñānadvaya</s>) is proclaimed as <s>samāpatti</s> (meditative attainment);
through the attainment of the two knowledges, by the method as described — || Pk 2.38 ||
whatever knowledge is obtained with effort, that is gained through the perception of light (<s>āloka</s>);

children.text: yasya vajrābjasaṃyogaḥ saṃvṛtyā tu na vidyate || Pk_2.39 ||
children.translated_text: he whose union of <s>vajra</s> and lotus does not exist conventionally — || Pk 2.39 ||
it is accomplished by the power of <s>yoga</s>, even for one who has experienced [it] once;

children.text: yathā prabhedaṃ vijñāya jñānavṛttiṃ svabhāvataḥ || Pk_2.40 ||
children.translated_text: having understood the distinctions, the activity of knowledge by its very nature — || Pk 2.40 ||

children.text: lakṣayet satataṃ yogī tāmeva prakṛtiṃ punaḥ |
children.translated_text: the <s>yogin</s> should constantly observe that very <s>prakṛti</s> (innate nature) again;
just as many clouds, of various shapes and colors, || Pk 2.41 ||
having arisen from the expanse of the sky, dissolve back into it —
so all the innate natures (<s>prakṛti</s>), whose causes are the three appearances (<s>ābhāsatraya</s>), || Pk 2.42 ||
having pervaded all sense-objects, enter the luminous (<s>prabhāsvara</s>);
those who are enveloped by the veil of not knowing the essential nature of these — || Pk 2.43 ||
having performed wholesome and unwholesome <s>karma</s>, they wander in the five destinies (<s>gatipañcaka</s>);
having committed the immediate [sins] (<s>ānantarya</s>) and such, [one] ripens in the hells; || Pk 2.44 ||
having performed wholesome [deeds] such as generosity (<s>dāna</s>) etc., [one] is exalted in the heavens and such;

children.text: anantajanmasāhasraṃ prāpya caivaṃ punaḥ punaḥ || Pk_2.45 ||
children.translated_text: having obtained infinite thousands of births, again and again — || Pk 2.45 ||
[one] grieves through delusion, [thinking] 'this is the ripening of prior <s>karma</s>';
that by which beings are afflicted through the union of the innate nature and appearances — || Pk 2.46 ||
knowing that very [nature], the knowers are liberated from the cage of existence;
this visualization of the moon-disc (<s>candramaṇḍala</s>) is itself of the nature of <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom); || Pk 2.47 ||
one should see the mind itself by itself, like the orb of the moon;

children.text: atha candraṃ samālambya vajracinhaṃ prakalpayet || Pk_2.48 ||
children.translated_text: then, relying on the moon, one should visualize the <s>vajra</s> sign; || Pk 2.48 ||
for this is the indicator of <s>upāya</s> (skillful means) for <s>yogins</s> of the generation [stage] beginning with <s>vajra</s>;
the union of moon, <s>vajra</s>, etc. is the coming together of <s>citta</s> (mind) and <s>caitta</s> (mental factors); || Pk 2.49 ||
from the union of <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom) and <s>upāya</s> (means), the form of the deity is born;
having sealed with the four <s>mudrās</s>, bearing the pride of the deity — || Pk 2.50 ||
the <s>mantrin</s> (practitioner) should always conduct himself as one who possesses the <s>yoga</s> of the generation stage (<s>utpattikrama</s>);

children.text: yathoktaṃ śrīsamājādau tatra tatra suvistaram || Pk_2.51 ||
children.translated_text: as described in the <s>Śrī-Samāja</s> [Tantra] and elsewhere, in detail in each [chapter] — || Pk 2.51 ||
as long as there is the <s>yoga</s> of meditation, so long is one a beginner (<s>ādikarmikaḥ</s>);
the indication of the perfected <s>yoga</s> is now being given. || Pk 2.52 ||
The purification of the three emptinesses (<s>śūnyatraya</s>) — that is here called the luminous (<s>prabhāsvara</s>);
and that state of complete emptiness (<s>sarvaśūnya</s>) [arises] from the purification of the three knowledges; || Pk 2.53 ||
the state of purification of knowledge — that reality (<s>tattva</s>) is the unsurpassed omniscience;

children.text: nirvikāraṃ nirābhāsaṃ nirdvandvaṃ paramaṃ śivam || Pk_2.54 ||
children.translated_text: unchanging, without appearance, free from duality, the supreme bliss (<s>śiva</s>); || Pk 2.54 ||

children.text: astīti na ca nāstīti na ca vākyagocaram |
children.translated_text: neither 'it exists' nor 'it does not exist,' nor within the range of speech;
therefore, from the purified luminous, arising from the three knowledges — || Pk 2.55 ||
bearing the thirty-two marks, endowed with the eighty minor characteristics,
possessed of all excellent forms — the omniscient one is born from that; || Pk 2.56 ||
and thus it is stated in the <s>Mahāyāna</s> <s>sūtra</s>, the <s>Lalitavistara</s>:
'This <s>Śākyasiṃha Tathāgata</s>, desiring perfect awakening — || Pk 2.57 ||
thinking "I shall attain <s>Buddhahood</s> through the great emptiness (<s>mahāśūnya</s>),"
on the bank of the <s>Nairañjanā</s> river, having accomplished [his practice], he entered into extreme asceticism; || Pk 2.58 ||
then, like mustard seeds packed full, the <s>Jinas</s> (Victorious Ones), stationed in the midst of space,
addressed him with a single voice — that son of the <s>Jinas</s> — clearly: || Pk 2.59 ||
"This meditation is impure, and it does not bring the desired result;
rather, relying on the luminous (<s>prabhāsvara</s>), the supreme, like the surface of space — || Pk 2.60 ||
when the state of the luminous is attained, you will be born in the form of your own wish;

children.text: savaiśvaryaṃ tathā prāpya vajrakāye pramodase || Pk_2.61 ||
children.translated_text: and having attained such sovereignty, you will rejoice in the <s>vajra</s>-body." || Pk 2.61 ||

children.text: evaṃ śrutvā tu taṃ śbdaṃ visarjyāsphānakaṃ tataḥ |
children.translated_text: Thus having heard that speech, abandoning extreme asceticism,
at the time of midnight, relying on the reality (<s>tattva</s>), that son of the <s>Jinas</s> — || Pk 2.62 ||
with body perfectly upright, and with speech also perfectly straight,

children.text: sāśano nāśano naiva na maunī nāpyamaunavān || Pk_2.63 ||
children.translated_text: neither with instruction nor without instruction, neither silent nor not silent — || Pk 2.63 ||
with eyes neither open wide nor closed,

children.text: svacchaṃ vyaktaṃ mahājñānaṃ sarvaśūnyaṃ mahādbhutam || Pk_2.64 ||
children.translated_text: clear, manifest, the great knowledge — completely empty, supremely wondrous; || Pk 2.64 ||
then he sees that manifest [reality], through the grace of the <s>guru</s>'s feet —
the future, the past, and the present — the three existences; || Pk 2.65 ||
in that very moment, he sees all, the holder of the purified luminous,
adorned with the qualities of illusion (<s>māyā</s>) — like the moon in water, mirages, etc.; || Pk 2.66 ||
at the time of dawn, through the <s>vajra</s>-like <s>samādhi</s>,
seated at the foot of the <s>Bodhi</s> [tree], he performed the subjugation of <s>Māra</s>; || Pk 2.67 ||
having attained, as the <s>Śākya</s> Lord, the unsurpassed knowledge of reality (<s>tattvajñāna</s>),
for the benefit of the three worlds, that very [knowledge] is here demonstrated; || Pk 2.68 ||
'Knowledge of reality' — thus is proclaimed the vision of perfect awakening (<s>abhisambodhi</s>);

children.text: pañcānantaryakarmā ca mandapuṇyo 'pi yo naraḥ || Pk_2.69 ||
children.translated_text: even a person who has committed the five immediate [sins] (<s>pañcānantarya</s>), of meager merit — || Pk 2.69 ||
obtains [it] through the <s>guru</s>'s grace, like a <s>cintāmaṇi</s> (wish-fulfilling jewel), supreme;
he performs conduct as he wishes — this [person] is a future fully-awakened <s>Buddha</s>; || Pk 2.70 ||

children.text: na rāgo na virāgaśca madhyamā nopalabhyate |
children.translated_text: neither passion nor dispassion — the middle is not apprehended;

children.text: na śūnyaṃ nāpi cāśūnyaṃ madhyamā nopalabhyate || Pk_2.71 ||
children.translated_text: neither empty nor non-empty — the middle is not apprehended; || Pk 2.71 ||
the union of all <s>Buddhas</s> — this very [teaching] has been demonstrated;

children.text: trijñānād vyatiriktaṃ yat tattvaṃ sandhyāya bhāṣayā || Pk_2.72 ||
children.translated_text: that reality which transcends the three knowledges — [expressed] in intentional language (<s>sandhyā bhāṣā</s>) — || Pk 2.72 ||
through verses beginning with 'in the absence,' in the chapter on <s>bodhicitta</s>;
in the <s>Śrī-Samāja</s> [Tantra] too, that characteristic of perfect awakening has been proclaimed; || Pk 2.73 ||
the purification of passion (<s>rāga</s>) and the rest, which was shown in the first [chapter],

children.text: sarvaśūnyaṃ samuddiśya sāpi proktā tathāgataiḥ || Pk_2.74 ||
children.translated_text: that too has been proclaimed by the <s>Tathāgatas</s> with reference to the state of complete emptiness; || Pk 2.74 ||
the reality that has been demonstrated in the various <s>sūtras</s> and <s>tantras</s>
is indeed this state of complete emptiness — nothing else is spoken of therein; || Pk 2.75 ||
in the eighty-four thousand <s>dharma</s>-aggregates (<s>dharmaskandha</s>) of the Great Sage,
the most essential of the essential has been proclaimed — the characteristic of perfect awakening; || Pk 2.76 ||
whether matted-haired, naked, shaven-headed, or with topknot — those of detached conduct,
with their various external signs — [all] desirous of perfect awakening; || Pk 2.77 ||
for those devoid of reality, the sequence of vows, conduct, and the like,
because of being devoid of the knowledge of reality — liberation is not obtained thereby; || Pk 2.78 ||
through the <s>yoga</s> of a beginner, one may attain the eighth <s>bhūmi</s> (stage);
and the seer of the three lights, established in the tenth <s>bhūmi</s> — || Pk 2.79 ||
having attained perfect awakening (<s>abhisambodhi</s>), [one] arrives at the pure abodes (<s>śuddhāvāsa</s>);
non-regressing (<s>avaivartī</s>) in the <s>Buddha</s>-fields, omniscient in this very life; || Pk 2.80 ||
the awakening of <s>dharmodaya</s> (arising of <s>dharma</s>) — through the details of play (<s>krīḍā</s>), passion, etc.;
the awakening of <s>dharmadhātu</s> (sphere of <s>dharma</s>) — through activities according to what is obtained; || Pk 2.81 ||
the unsurpassed awakening — through the <s>yoga</s> of perfect awakening;
through conduct of elaborate forms etc. — <s>yogins</s> practice here; || Pk 2.82 ||
'Ah! What [need] for the <s>yoga</s> of practice? The primordial purity is innate;

children.text: prakṛtyaiva hi sā siddhā tathatā na vikalpajā || Pk_2.83 ||
children.translated_text: that <s>tathatā</s> (suchness) is indeed accomplished by [its own] nature — it is not born of conceptual construction.' || Pk 2.83 ||
Those who thus construct [such views] here, abandoning the stages of knowledge,

children.text: tatprabhedamajānānāḥ punaḥ śaikṣā bhavanti te || Pk_2.84 ||
children.translated_text: not knowing its distinctions — they become trainees (<s>śaikṣa</s>) again; || Pk 2.84 ||
those who know the distinctions of the innate nature and appearances, who resort to the fourth reality,

children.text: tridhā nābhyasyate yastu na śīghramāpnuyāt phalam || Pk_2.85 ||
children.translated_text: but do not practice the threefold [path] — they do not quickly obtain the fruit; || Pk 2.85 ||
just as fire, latent in wood, does not rise without churning,

children.text: tathābhyāsād binā bodhirjāyate neha janmani || Pk_2.86 ||
children.translated_text: so without practice, awakening (<s>bodhi</s>) is not born in this life; || Pk 2.86 ||

children.text: yaḥ śāṭhyabuddhiralaso gurunindakaśca prāptābhiṣeka iti garvitamānasaḥ syāt |
children.translated_text: one who is deceitful-minded, lazy, and a reviler of the <s>guru</s>, who, having received <s>abhiṣeka</s> (initiation), becomes proud-minded —

children.text: sarvajñatā na sulabheti vihīnacitto doṣān sa paśyati gurorna guṇān varākaḥ || Pk_2.87 ||
children.translated_text: [thinking] 'omniscience is not easily attained,' that wretched one, of degraded mind, sees faults in the <s>guru</s>, not virtues; || Pk 2.87 ||

children.text: sūśrūṣayā virahito laghu tattvamicchen neti praśstavacanaṃ calayet saroṣaḥ |
children.translated_text: devoid of devotion (<s>śuśrūṣā</s>), he would easily [seek] the reality; he angrily agitates [against] the praise-worthy words [of the <s>guru</s>];

children.text: dṛṣṭvā sabhāsu gurumasya parāṅmukhastu kuryāt praṇāmamatha tasya rahogatasya || Pk_2.88 ||
children.translated_text: seeing the <s>guru</s> in assemblies, turning his face away, he would make obeisance [only] when [the <s>guru</s>] is in private; || Pk 2.88 ||
such a wicked bad disciple — even if one's own legitimate son, [he is] blameworthy among the noble —

children.text: vaiśyaṃ tathā pārthivamagrabodhiṃ kuryāt samīpe na hi jātu dhīraḥ || Pk_2.89 ||
children.translated_text: whether a <s>vaiśya</s> or a king, [even if] foremost in awakening — the wise one should never place [such a person] nearby; || Pk 2.89 ||

children.text: śubhaguṇasusameto jñānavān vīryayukto gurujanamatha bhaktyā vīkṣate buddhatulyam |
children.translated_text: one who is well-endowed with good qualities, possessed of knowledge, joined with vigor, who regards the <s>guru</s>-folk with devotion as equal to the <s>Buddha</s>,

children.text: adhigatajinadharmaḥ śāsaneṣu prasannaḥ sa iha bhavati pātraṃ tasya kuryāt prasādam || Pk_2.90 ||
children.translated_text: who has realized the <s>dharma</s> of the <s>Jinas</s>, who is devoted to the teachings — he is a worthy vessel here; one should bestow grace upon him; || Pk 2.90 ||
one who has studied many <s>tantras</s>, skilled in the <s>āgamas</s>, but who has not obtained instruction through serving the <s>guru</s>-folk —

children.text: svahitamapi sa kartuṃ na prabhuḥ śāstracañcurbhavati tadapi śāstraṃ kevalaṃ khedahetuḥ || Pk_2.91 ||
children.translated_text: he is unable to accomplish even his own benefit; though clever in <s>śāstra</s>, that <s>śāstra</s> [study] is merely a cause of fatigue; || Pk 2.91 ||

children.text: atha bhavati sabhāgyaḥ prāptatattvopadeśo jaḍamatirasamartho mīlane 'rthasya yastu |
children.translated_text: but if one is fortunate, having obtained instruction in the reality, yet dull-witted and incapable of penetrating the meaning —
One who, with a mind devoted to the welfare of others, has engaged in teaching, yet is devoid of the virtues of speech — he too incurs contempt. || Pk 2.92 ||
One who has studied many tantras, is learned, skilled like a bee [in extracting essence], endowed with memory, intelligence, fortitude, and the wealth of vigor,

children.text: gurucaṇasaparyāprāptatattvopadeśaḥ prabhavati sa hi vaktuṃ tantrarājopadeśam || Pk_2.93 ||
children.translated_text: who has received the instruction in reality through the worship of the guru's feet — he is able to teach the instruction of the king of tantras. || Pk 2.93 ||

body.text:
śrutabahutaratantreṇāyavajriprasādāt sphuṭaviracitavācā bodhimārgaṃ vibhajya |
kuśalamupacittaṃ yacchākyamitreṇa tena prakaṭapaṭuvipākād bodhibhājo bhavantu || iti | Pk_2.94 ||
body.translated_text: By <s>Śākyamitra</s>, who has studied many tantras, through the grace of the <s>Vajra</s>-lord, with clearly composed words, having distinguished the path to awakening — may they become partakers of enlightenment through the clearly matured result of the merit accumulated by him. || Pk 2.94 ||
Also known as the <s>Anuttarasandhi</s> (Supreme Union).
|| The <s>Sarvaśuddhiviśuddhikrama</s> (Stage of Complete Purification) is completed. ||
This is the work of the venerable <s>Śākyamitra</s>. The extent of the text is one hundred [verses].
The second stage.
[3] The <s>Svādhiṣṭhānakrama</s> (Stage of Self-Consecration), the third.
Homage to the glorious <s>Vajraguru</s>.

children.translated_text: Having bowed to the excellent <s>Vajra</s>, the leader beginning with <s>Vajrasattva</s>,
the <s>Svādhiṣṭhānakrama</s> (Stage of Self-Consecration) will now be expounded by me, out of compassion. || Pk 3.1 ||

body.text: prathamataraṃ tāvad utpattikramānusāreṇa prāptābhiṣekaścaturvidhatantrābhiprāyajñaḥ prāptakāyavākcittavivekaḥ śrutidharaḥ satyadvayādhimokṣo vajraguruṃ samyag ārādhya, tataḥ prasannāya gurave mahatīṃ gaṇapūjāṃ kṛtvā ṣoḍaśābdikāṃ mudrāṃ mahāvajragurave datvā, tadanantaraṃ guruvaktrād āptasvādhiṣṭhānakramopadeśaḥ, tato mālodakasambuddhavajraghaṇṭādānadarpaṇanāmācāryānujñā ityebhiḥ saha guhyābhiṣekaṃ labdhvā ebhiḥ śāstāraṃ guruṃ stūyātḥ |
body.translated_text: First of all, in accordance with the <s>utpattikrama</s> (generation stage), one who has received <s>abhiṣeka</s> (initiation), who knows the intent of the fourfold tantra, who has attained the isolation of body, speech, and mind, who retains what is heard, who has conviction in the two truths — having properly propitiated the <s>vajraguru</s>, then, having performed a great communal offering (<s>gaṇapūjā</s>) for the pleased guru, having given a sixteen-year-old <s>mudrā</s> (consort) to the great <s>vajraguru</s>, and thereupon having received from the guru's mouth the instruction in the <s>Svādhiṣṭhānakrama</s>, then having obtained the secret initiation (<s>guhyābhiṣeka</s>) together with the garland-water, the awakened <s>vajra</s>-bell, the giving of the mirror, and the name-teacher's permission — one should praise the guru as teacher with these [verses]:

children.text: śauṣīryaṃ nāsti te kāye māṃsāsthirudhiraṃ na ca |
children.translated_text: There is no hollowness in your body, nor flesh, bone, or blood;
like a rainbow in the sky, you have displayed your body. || Pk 3.2 ||

children.text: nāmayā nāśuciḥ kāye kṣuttṛṣṇāsambhavo na ca |
children.translated_text: No disease, no impurity in your body, no arising of hunger and thirst;

children.text: tvayā lokānuvṛttyarthaṃ darśitā laukikī kriyā || Pk_3.3 ||
children.translated_text: by you, for the purpose of conforming to the world, worldly activity has been displayed. || Pk 3.3 ||
Like the moon in water, ungraspable, not established in any <s>dharma</s>,

children.text: anahaṅkāra nirmoha nirālamba namo 'stu te || Pk_3.4 ||
children.translated_text: without ego, without delusion, without support — homage to you! || Pk 3.4 ||
You are always in <s>samādhi</s> (meditative absorption), whether walking, standing, or sleeping;

children.text: īrṣyāpatheṣu sarveṣu nirālamba namo 'stu te || Pk_3.5 ||
children.translated_text: on all the paths of the sense-fields, without support — homage to you! || Pk 3.5 ||
You manifest miraculous transformations by great supernatural power, through illusion-like <s>samādhi</s>;

children.text: nirnānātvaṃ samāpanna nirālamba namostu te || Pk_3.6 ||
children.translated_text: having attained the state beyond all multiplicity, without support — homage to you! || Pk 3.6 ||

body.text: evaṃ vajraguraṃ sadbhūtaguṇena saṃstutya śravaṇārtham adhyeṣayed anayā gāthayā-
body.translated_text: Having thus praised the <s>vajraguru</s> with his true qualities, one should request [the teaching] for the purpose of hearing, with this verse —

children.translated_text: O <s>Sarvajña</s> (Omniscient One), mass of wisdom, purifier of the wheel of existence,

children.text: adya vyākhyānaratnena prasādaṃ kuru me vibho || Pk_3.7 ||
children.translated_text: today, by the jewel of exposition, bestow your grace upon me, O Lord! || Pk 3.7 ||
Apart from the lotus of your feet, there is no other refuge, O Lord;

children.text: tasmāt prasīda buddhāgra jagadvīra mahāmune || Pk_3.8 ||
children.translated_text: therefore, be gracious, O foremost of <s>Buddhas</s>, hero of the world, O great sage! || Pk 3.8 ||

children.text: evaṃ śrutvā tu tad vākyam adhyeṣaṇaviśāradam |
children.translated_text: Having heard that speech, skilled in supplication,
generating compassion for the disciple, one should then begin the self-consecration (<s>svādhiṣṭhāna</s>). || Pk 3.9 ||
The <s>Svādhiṣṭhānakrama</s> is the seeing of the truth of the conventional (<s>saṃvṛti</s>);
it is obtained through the grace of the guru's feet and not otherwise. || Pk 3.10 ||
The practitioner (<s>sādhaka</s>) who does not obtain the <s>Svādhiṣṭhānakrama</s> —
his effort in <s>sūtra</s>, tantra, and <s>kalpa</s> texts is in vain. || Pk 3.11 ||
Having obtained the <s>Svādhiṣṭhānakrama</s>, the lord who is of the nature of all <s>Buddhas</s>
attains Buddhahood without doubt in this very life. || Pk 3.12 ||
The <s>samādhi</s> of self-consecration (<s>svādhiṣṭhāna</s>) and the state of <s>prabhāsvara</s> (clear light) —
these are known as the two truths (<s>satyadvaya</s>), by the distinction of fruit and cause. || Pk 3.13 ||
Through the sequence of self-consecration, the clear light (<s>prabhāsvara</s>) is attained;

children.text: tasmād vajraguruḥ pūrvaṃ svādhiṣṭhānaṃ pradarśayet || Pk_3.14 ||
children.translated_text: therefore, the <s>vajraguru</s> should first demonstrate the self-consecration. || Pk 3.14 ||

children.text: asvatantraṃ jagat sarvaṃ svatantraṃ naiva jāyate |
children.translated_text: The entire world is not self-dependent; nothing whatsoever arises independently;

children.text: hetuḥ prabhāsvaraṃ tasya sarvaśūnyaṃ prabhāsvaram || Pk_3.15 ||
children.translated_text: the clear light is the cause of that [world]; the clear light is completely empty (<s>sarvaśūnya</s>). || Pk 3.15 ||

children.text: yena cittena bālāśca saṃsāre bandhanaṃ gatāḥ |
children.translated_text: By that very mind by which the childish ones have gone into bondage in <s>saṃsāra</s>,

children.text: yoginastena cittena sugatānāṃ gatiṃ gatāḥ || Pk_3.16 ||
children.translated_text: by that very mind, the yogins have gone to the state of the <s>Sugatas</s> (Buddhas). || Pk 3.16 ||

children.text: na cātrotpadyate kaścin maraṇaṃ nāpi kasyacit |
children.translated_text: Neither does anyone arise here, nor is there death for anyone;
<s>saṃsāra</s> itself is to be understood as established in the form and appearance of mind. || Pk 3.17 ||
Without the yoga of <s>vāyu</s> (wind/breath), the true nature of mind is not grasped;
from the mind, because it is the cause of [primordial] nature, arise <s>karma</s> (action) and birth. || Pk 3.18 ||
That very [mind], conjoined with <s>vāyu</s> (wind), [becomes] again the triad of consciousness (<s>vijñānatritaya</s>);
the form of yogins is born [from it] — that is called the <s>māyādeha</s> (illusion-body). || Pk 3.19 ||
Therefore, the entire world is said to be like an illusion (<s>māyopama</s>);
one established in illusion-like <s>samādhi</s> sees everything as such. || Pk 3.20 ||

children.text: rūpaṃ ca vedanā caiva saṃjñā saṃskāra eva ca |
children.translated_text: Form, feeling,

children.text: vijñānaṃ pañcamaṃ caiva catvāro dhātavastathā || Pk_3.21 ||
children.translated_text: perception, formations, and consciousness as the fifth, and likewise the four elements, || Pk 3.21 ||
the sense-faculties and sense-objects, and the five kinds of knowledge —

children.text: adhyātmabāhyato bhinnaṃ sarvaṃ māyaiva nānyathā || Pk_3.22 ||
children.translated_text: all that is divided into internal and external is nothing but illusion (<s>māyā</s>), not otherwise. || Pk 3.22 ||
One should perceive the illusion-body through a reflection in a mirror,
the colors through a rainbow, and the pervasiveness through the moon in water. || Pk 3.23 ||
Just as in a clear mirror, a reflection is clearly seen,
<s>Vajrasattva</s>, beautifully depicted, is free from both existence and non-existence. || Pk 3.24 ||
Endowed with all excellent aspects, with a form that is never repulsive —

children.text: darśayet taṃ suśiṣyāya svādhiṣṭhānaṃ taducyate || Pk_3.25 ||
children.translated_text: one should show that to a worthy disciple; that is called self-consecration (<s>svādhiṣṭhāna</s>). || Pk 3.25 ||
This indeed is the illusion (<s>māyā</s>) to be observed, having the characteristic of being faultless;

children.text: māyaiva saṃvṛteḥ satyaṃ kāyaḥ sāmbhogikaśca saḥ || Pk_3.26 ||
children.translated_text: illusion itself is the truth of the conventional (<s>saṃvṛti</s>), and that [body] is the <s>sāṃbhogikakāya</s> (enjoyment body). || Pk 3.26 ||

children.text: saiva gandharvasattvaḥ syād vajrakāyaḥ sa eva hi |
children.translated_text: That very one would be a <s>gandharvasattva</s> (celestial being), and that indeed is the <s>vajrakāya</s> (diamond body);

children.text: vajrasattvaḥ svayaṃ tasmāt svasya pūjāṃ pravartayet || Pk_3.27 ||
children.translated_text: therefore, being <s>Vajrasattva</s> himself, one should perform worship of oneself. || Pk 3.27 ||
The self is indeed all Buddhahood and all lordship as well;

children.text: tasmāt sarvaprayatnena hyātmānaṃ pūjayet sadā || Pk_3.28 ||
children.translated_text: therefore, with all effort, one should always worship the self. || Pk 3.28 ||
The application of <s>mantras</s> and <s>mudrās</s>, the visualization of <s>maṇḍalas</s> and the like,

children.text: balihomakriryāṃ sarvāṃ kuryān māyopamāṃ sadā || Pk_3.29 ||
children.translated_text: all rituals of offerings (<s>bali</s>) and fire-oblations (<s>homa</s>) — one should always perform [them] as illusion-like. || Pk 3.29 ||
Pacifying (<s>śāntika</s>) and prosperity-bringing (<s>pauṣṭika</s>) [rites], as well as subjugation (<s>vaśya</s>) and destructive (<s>ābhicārika</s>) [rites],

children.text: ākarṣaṇādi yat sarvaṃ kuryād indrāyudhopamam || Pk_3.30 ||
children.translated_text: attraction (<s>ākarṣaṇa</s>) and all such [rites] — one should perform [them] as rainbow-like. || Pk 3.30 ||
The enjoyment of erotic pleasure (<s>śṛṅgāra</s>) and the like, the practice of song, music, and the rest,

children.text: kalāsu ca pravṛttiṃ ca kuryād udakacandravat || Pk_3.31 ||
children.translated_text: and the engagement in the arts — one should perform [them] as moon-in-water-like. || Pk 3.31 ||

children.text: rūpe śabde tathā gandhe rase spraṣṭavya eva ca |
children.translated_text: In form, sound, smell,
taste, and touch — one should perceive the engagement of the eye and other [senses] as illusion-like. || Pk 3.32 ||
What more need be said here? In the <s>Vajrayāna</s>, in truth,

children.text: yad yad ālambayed yogī tad tad māyaiva kalpayet || Pk_3.33 ||
children.translated_text: whatever the yogin takes as object, he should regard all that as nothing but illusion. || Pk 3.33 ||

children.text: darpaṇe pratibimbaṃ ca svapnaṃ māyāṃ ca budbudam |
children.translated_text: A reflection in a mirror, a dream, an illusion, a bubble,

children.text: indrajālaṃ ca sādṛśyaṃ yaḥ paśyed sa prabhuḥ smṛtaḥ || Pk_3.34 ||
children.translated_text: a magic show, and a likeness — whoever sees [thus] is remembered as a lord. || Pk 3.34 ||

body.text:
dṛśyate spṛśyate caiva yathā māyā jagat sadā |
na copalambhaḥ saṃvṛtyā māyāvat parikīrtitaḥ || iti || Pk_3.35 ||
body.translated_text: The world is always seen and touched, just like an illusion; and there is no apprehension [of it as real] — it is proclaimed to be like an illusion, conventionally. || Pk 3.35 ||

children.text: yad yad indriyamārgatvaṃ māyā tattat svabhāvataḥ |
children.translated_text: Whatever is the path of the senses — all of that is illusion by its very nature;
through the yoga of non-concentration, one should bear everything as being of the nature of all <s>Buddhas</s>. || Pk 3.36 ||

children.text: sarvatra sarvataḥ sarvaṃ sarvathā sarvadā svayam |
children.translated_text: Everywhere, in all ways, everything, in every manner, always, by oneself —

children.text: sarvabuddhamayaṃ siddhaṃ svamātmānaṃ sa paśyati || Pk_3.37 ||
children.translated_text: he sees his own self as accomplished, pervaded by all <s>Buddhas</s>. || Pk 3.37 ||
Walking and standing, the great being (<s>mahāsattva</s>), the lord filled with all happiness,
obtains dwelling, food, drink, and the rest from space in an instant. || Pk 3.38 ||
May they be cutters of [the cycle of] existence, teachers among the supreme people;

children.text: pūjyante sasuraiḥ sarvaiḥ praṇipatya muhurmuhuḥ || Pk_3.39 ||
children.translated_text: they are worshipped by all, including the gods, who bow again and again. || Pk 3.39 ||
Just as [it is] when a teacher is connected, who seeks the welfare of worldly life,
so too is the great yogin, through the collection of universal knowledge and purpose. || Pk 3.40 ||

children.text: nāsti kiñcid asādhyaṃ vai vajrasattvena lakṣitam |
children.translated_text: There is nothing whatsoever that cannot be accomplished, marked by <s>Vajrasattva</s>;
all <s>mudrās</s> of great bliss (<s>mahāsukha</s>) are spontaneously accomplished by themselves. || Pk 3.41 ||

children.text: kleśāḥ karmapathā dehaḥ kartāraśca phalaṃ ca vai |
children.translated_text: The <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions), the paths of <s>karma</s>, the body, the agents, and the fruit —
[all are] like a mirage, like a dream, like a <s>gandharva</s> city (celestial city). || Pk 3.42 ||
Not knowing this <s>samādhi</s>, through apprehension in the conventional [level],

children.text: jāyante vividhā rogāsteṣāṃ māyā bhiṣagjitam || Pk_3.43 ||
children.translated_text: various diseases arise — for them, illusion is the victorious physician. || Pk 3.43 ||
One who does not obtain the instruction in self-consecration from the guru,

children.text: śāśvatocchedamālambya sa vaivartī bhavet punaḥ || Pk_3.44 ||
children.translated_text: clinging to eternalism or nihilism, he becomes a backslider again. || Pk 3.44 ||
Abandoning all [other] worship, one should commence the worship of the guru;
by his being pleased, that supreme knowledge of the omniscient one is obtained. || Pk 3.45 ||

children.text: kiṃ tena na kṛtaṃ puṇyaṃ kiṃ vā nopāsitaṃ tapaḥ |
children.translated_text: What merit has not been performed, what austerity has not been practiced
by [one who performs] the unsurpassed worship of the teacher <s>Vajrasattva</s>? || Pk 3.46 ||
Whatever is most desired and most distinguished —

children.text: tat taddhi gurave deyaṃ tadevākṣayamicchatā || Pk_3.47 ||
children.translated_text: That indeed should be given to the <s>guru</s> (teacher) by one who desires the imperishable. (Pk 3.47)

children.text: ācāryo harate pāpam ācāryo harate bhayam |
children.translated_text: The <s>ācārya</s> (master) removes sin, the <s>ācārya</s> removes fear;
the <s>ācārya</s> carries one across to the far shore, from the great terror of the ocean of suffering. (Pk 3.48)
One who is smeared with the impurity of ego, who violates the true stages (<s>sadbhūtakrama</s>),

children.text: sāvajñastattvadharmeṣu tasya tattvaṃ na darśayet || Pk_3.49 ||
children.translated_text: who is disrespectful toward the doctrines of reality — to him one should not reveal the truth. (Pk 3.49)
One who is truthful in speech, devoted to the <s>guru</s>, solitary, and of single-pointed resolve,

children.text: samayācārarakṣī ca kramaṃ tasya pradarśayet || Pk_3.50 ||
children.translated_text: who guards the observances of the <s>samaya</s> (vow) — to him one should demonstrate the stages (<s>krama</s>). (Pk 3.50)

body.translated_text: Thus ends the third [chapter], the <s>Svādhiṣṭhānakrama</s> (Stage of Self-Empowerment).
This is the composition of the venerable master <s>Nāgārjuna</s>. The extent of this text is fifty-six [verses].
[4] The fourth: <s>Abhisambodhikrama</s> (Stage of Perfect Awakening)
Homage to the glorious <s>Vajrasattva</s>!

children.translated_text: Having bowed to <s>Vajrasattva</s>, the teacher of universal emptiness (<s>sarvaśūnya</s>),
this fourth <s>Abhisambodhikrama</s> (Stage of Perfect Awakening) shall be expounded by me. (Pk 4.1)
That self-existent (<s>svayambhū</s>) <s>Bhagavān</s> (Blessed One) is the sole supreme deity;
but due to bestowing instruction, the <s>vajrācārya</s> (vajra-master) is superior even to him. (Pk 4.2)
Having performed devotion to him for a year, or even a month,

children.text: tasmai tuṣṭāya gurave pūjāṃ kuryāt tu śaktitaḥ || Pk_4.3 ||
children.translated_text: to that pleased <s>guru</s>, one should make offerings according to one's ability. (Pk 4.3)
Having presented to him the <s>mudrā</s> (seal/consort) according to its true nature, well-trained,

children.text: gaṇamaṇḍalamadhye tu kuryāt pūjāṃ yathāvidhi || Pk_4.4 ||
children.translated_text: in the midst of the <s>gaṇamaṇḍala</s> (assembly circle), one should perform worship according to the prescribed rite. (Pk 4.4)
Then the great <s>yogī</s>, pleased by the enjoyment of the five sense-pleasures,
should cause the arising of the light (<s>āloka</s>) through the method of <s>samāpatti</s> (meditative attainment). (Pk 4.5)
Having carefully established the <s>bodhicitta</s> (awakening mind) in a ritual vessel (<s>kalaśa</s>) and so forth,

children.text: ardharātre cābhisiñcet suśiṣyaṃ kṛpayā guruḥ || Pk_4.6 ||
children.translated_text: at midnight, the <s>guru</s> should consecrate the worthy disciple with compassion. (Pk 4.6)
Having received the <s>abhiṣeka</s> (consecration), again at dawn,
the disciple, with palms joined, should worship and propitiate the <s>guru</s> with hymns of praise. (Pk 4.7)
You who are liberated from the three realms (<s>traidhātuka</s>), who have attained equality with space,

children.text: nopariṣyasi kāmeṣu nirālamba namo 'stu te || Pk_4.8 ||
children.translated_text: you shall not fall into sensual desires — homage to you, O supportless one (<s>nirālamba</s>)! (Pk 4.8)
You are unattached to the <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates), <s>dhātus</s> (elements), and <s>āyatanas</s> (sense-bases);
liberated from false views (<s>viparyāsa</s>) — homage to you, O supportless one! (Pk 4.9)
O you of unconstructed intention, of unestablished mind,
of inconceivable mental engagement — homage to you, O supportless one! (Pk 4.10)
Without foundation, like space, free from conceptual elaboration (<s>niṣprapañca</s>), untainted,
your mind is equal to space — homage to you, O supportless one! (Pk 4.11)
Desiring to see perfect awakening (<s>abhisambodhi</s>), which is of the nature of universal emptiness,

children.text: stutvā kṛtāñjaliḥ śiṣyo guraṃ sañcodayet punaḥ || Pk_4.12 ||
children.translated_text: having praised [thus], the disciple with palms joined should again urge the <s>guru</s>: (Pk 4.12)
'Grant me, O great protector, the vision of perfect awakening,
freed from the bondage of <s>karma</s> and birth, devoid of the three appearances. (Pk 4.13)
Grant me, O great <s>ācārya</s>, the supreme <s>vajrajñāna</s> (adamantine wisdom),
the great wisdom of all <s>Buddhas</s>, the abode of all <s>Tathāgatas</s>. (Pk 4.14)
Grant me, O great <s>Vajra</s>, the purification of body, speech, and mind,
beginningless and endless, peaceful, the purifier of all <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions).' (Pk 4.15)
The <s>yogī</s>, thus propitiated by the proclamation of true qualities,
having generated compassion toward the disciple, should then commence the stage thus: (Pk 4.16)
The light (<s>āloka</s>) is the night portion; the clear rays of the sun would be the daylight radiance;
the twilight light is obtained — it is repeatedly joined with the natural [states] (<s>prakṛti</s>);

children.text: no rātrirnāpi sandhyā na ca bhavati divā yaḥ prakṛtyā vimuktaḥ
children.translated_text: it is neither night, nor twilight, nor does day arise — one who is liberated by nature,

children.text: sa syād bodhikṣaṇo 'yaṃ varagurukathito yogināmeva gamyaḥ || Pk_4.17 ||
children.translated_text: that would be this moment of awakening (<s>bodhikṣaṇa</s>), taught by the excellent <s>guru</s>, accessible only to <s>yogīs</s>. (Pk 4.17)

body.text:
naiśaṃ dhvāntaṃ vinaṣṭaṃ vyapagatamakhilaṃ sāndhyatejastu yasmin
bhāsvānnodeti yāvat kṣaṇa iha vimale darśayed bhūtakoṭim |
body.translated_text: The darkness of night is destroyed, all twilight radiance has departed; in that [moment] when the brilliant [sun] has not yet risen — in this pure instant, one should reveal the ultimate point of reality (<s>bhūtakoṭi</s>);

children.translated_text: to the disciple, the chief <s>ācārya</s>, having dispelled the darkness through the vision of external awakening,
attains inner bliss, free from defilement — the awakening of a <s>Buddha</s>, in an instant. (Pk 4.18)
Whether beginningless or having a beginning, whether without a middle or having a middle,

children.text: anantabhūtaṃ tvathavāntabhūtaṃ tat sarvaśūnyaṃ pravadanti santaḥ || Pk_4.19 ||
children.translated_text: whether endless or having an end — the wise declare all that to be empty (<s>sarvaśūnya</s>). (Pk 4.19)

children.text: gamanāgamanaṃ ca yatra nāsti kṣayavṛddhī na cāpyabhāvabhāvau |
children.translated_text: Where there is neither going nor coming, neither decay nor growth, neither non-existence nor existence,

children.text: ativismayarūpam arūpyavismayaṃ sthitimannāpi na cāpi gatvaram || Pk_4.20 ||
children.translated_text: of a form of supreme wonder, a formless wonder, neither stationary nor moving — (Pk 4.20)

children.text: yadasti-nāstivyavahāramuktaṃ na puṇyarūpaṃ na ca pāparūpam |
children.translated_text: that which is free from the conventions of 'exists' and 'does not exist,' neither of the form of merit nor of the form of sin,

children.text: na puṇyapāpātmakamagrabhūtaṃ tat sarvaśūnyaṃ pravadanti buddhāḥ || Pk_4.21 ||
children.translated_text: neither constituted by merit and sin, nor the primordial being — the <s>Buddhas</s> declare all that to be empty. (Pk 4.21)
Having attained such reality, the <s>yogī</s>, whose self is the animate and inanimate, the sole kinsman of the world,

children.text: yaḥ paryaṭejjñānamayo nṛsiṃhaḥ kṛtsnaṃ jagat so 'vyayakāyalābhī || Pk_4.22 ||
children.translated_text: who wanders [everywhere], composed of wisdom, a lion among men — he obtains the imperishable body. (Pk 4.22)
Though his body is perishable, he is of imperishable body; though without a seat, he is steadfast in the bond of the posture (<s>āsana</s>);

children.text: samīlitākṣo 'pi vibuddhanetraḥ samāhitaḥ sanna samāhitau'sau || Pk_4.23 ||
children.translated_text: though his eyes are closed, his eye is awakened; he is concentrated, yet not in concentration. (Pk 4.23)

children.text: sa vāgyuto vāgasamanvito 'pi bhogānvitaḥ so 'pi virupavṛttiḥ |
children.translated_text: He is endowed with speech, yet without speech; endowed with enjoyments, yet of formless conduct;

children.text: sa lokanāthaḥ parabhṛtyabhūto yastattvavit kṣīṇasamastadoṣaḥ || Pk_4.24 ||
children.translated_text: he is a lord of the world, yet become a servant of others — he who knows reality, in whom all faults are extinguished. (Pk 4.24)
The disciple who has received instruction should then practice <s>yoga</s> in two ways:
by the method of aggregate apprehension (<s>piṇḍagrāha</s>), and likewise by the method of analytical division (<s>anubheda</s>). (Pk 4.25)
From the head and from the feet, as far as the heart,

children.text: bhūtakoṭiṃ viśed yogī piṇḍagrāha iti smṛtaḥ || Pk_4.26 ||
children.translated_text: the <s>yogī</s> should enter the ultimate point of reality (<s>bhūtakoṭi</s>) — this is known as aggregate apprehension (<s>piṇḍagrāha</s>). (Pk 4.26)

children.text: sthāvaraṃ jaṅgamaṃ caiva pūrvaṃ kṛtvā prabhāsvaram |
children.translated_text: Having first made the stationary and the moving luminous (<s>prabhāsvara</s>),

children.text: paścāt kuryāt tathātmānam anubhedakramo hyayam || Pk_4.27 ||
children.translated_text: afterward one should make oneself likewise — this is the stage of analytical division (<s>anubhedakrama</s>). (Pk 4.27)
Just as breath-wind dissolves completely in a mirror,

children.text: bhūtakoṭiṃ tathā yogī praviśocca muhurmuhuḥ || Pk_4.28 ||
children.translated_text: so the <s>yogī</s> should enter the ultimate point of reality (<s>bhūtakoṭi</s>) again and again. (Pk 4.28)
Walking, standing, sleeping, eating, opening the eyes, closing the eyes, laughing —

children.text: anena dhyānayogena sadā tiṣṭhati tattvavit || Pk_4.29 ||
children.translated_text: through this method of <s>dhyāna</s>-<s>yoga</s> (meditative union), the knower of reality always abides [in that state]. (Pk 4.29)
The benefit of beings may sometimes arise, through rays of corresponding resemblance,
by means of the <s>Svādhiṣṭhānakrama</s> (Stage of Self-Empowerment), conjoined with wind and consciousness. (Pk 4.30)
Just as a fish quickly rises from the clear water of a river,
so from the clear universal emptiness, the net of magical illusion (<s>māyājāla</s>) is produced. (Pk 4.31)
The creation of <s>mahāmudrā</s> (great seal) and so forth, dependent on the five <s>Buddha</s> families,
rises up with five-colored rays, like <s>Indra's</s> bow (rainbow) in the sky. (Pk 4.32)

children.text: mudrābandhaṃ prakuryād vā mantraṃ cāpi japed yadi |
children.translated_text: Whether one forms the <s>mudrā</s>-bond (seal-gesture), or recites the <s>mantra</s>,
one may perform all other [activities] as well, while abiding in the state of universal emptiness. (Pk 4.33)
Eating all, cleaning all, saluting all, going everywhere,

children.text: sarvakṛt sarvaliṅgī ca sarvaśūnyena sidhyati || Pk_4.34 ||
children.translated_text: doing all, bearing all emblems — [all] is accomplished through universal emptiness (<s>sarvaśūnya</s>). (Pk 4.34)

children.text: prāptopadeśaḥ subhagaḥ suśiṣyo baudhau hi cittaṃ paramārthanāma |
children.translated_text: The fortunate disciple who has received instruction should again receive, in the <s>Buddha</s>-awakening, the mind [called] the supreme reality (<s>paramārtha</s>),
from the presence of the <s>guru</s>, with palms joined, holding flowers in hand: (Pk 4.35)

body.text: sarvabhāvavigataṃ skandhadhātvāyatanagrāhyagrāhakavarjitaṃ dharmanairātmyasamatayā svacittam ādyanutpannaṃ śūnyatāsvabhāvamiti |
body.translated_text: [Namely:] 'One's own mind, devoid of all entities, free from the grasped and the grasper of <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates), <s>dhātus</s> (elements), and <s>āyatanas</s> (sense-bases), through the equality of the selflessness of phenomena (<s>dharmanairātmya</s>), is primordially unborn, of the nature of emptiness (<s>śūnyatā</s>).'

children.translated_text: Then one should give to the <s>guru</s> a fitting offering (<s>dakṣiṇā</s>):

children.text: ratnaṃ gṛhaṃ vā hastyaśvaṃ grāmaṃ vā śayanāsanam || Pk_4.36 ||
children.translated_text: a jewel, or a house, an elephant, a horse, or a village, or a bed and seat. (Pk 4.36)

children.text: dāsaṃ dāsīṃ priyāṃ bhāryāṃ putrīṃ cāpyativarṇabhām |
children.translated_text: A male servant, a female servant, a beloved wife, a most beautiful daughter,
and even oneself — if one gives [all] that, what else remains? (Pk 4.37)
Having obtained the grace of the <s>ācārya</s>, with a mind pure and firm, [realizing] the inherent nature of all entities,
the clear, pure, extremely subtle, supremely auspicious <s>Buddha-nirvāṇa</s> realm,
free from dualities, free from conceptual construction, perpetually blissful — the <s>tattva-yogī</s> (practitioner of reality) should meditate [upon this];

children.text: puṇyāpuṇyād vimuktaḥ svayamiha bhagavān jāyate vajrasattvaḥ || Pk_4.38 ||
children.translated_text: liberated from merit and demerit, [the practitioner] himself here becomes the <s>Bhagavān</s> (Blessed One) <s>Vajrasattva</s>. (Pk 4.38)

body.translated_text: Thus ends the fourth [chapter], the <s>Abhisambodhikrama</s> (Stage of Perfect Awakening), the supreme secret of bliss.
This is the composition of the venerable master <s>Nāgārjuna</s>. The extent of this text is forty verses.
[5] The fifth: <s>Yuganaddhakrama</s> (Stage of Union)
Homage to the glorious <s>Vajradhara</s>!

children.translated_text: Having bowed to the Lord who is of the nature of fruit and cause, free from all dualities,
the supreme <s>Yuganaddhakrama</s> (Stage of Union) is correctly written [here]. (Pk 5.1)
By abandoning the dual conceptual construction of '<s>saṃsāra</s> (cyclic existence)' and '<s>nirvṛti</s> (cessation),'

children.text: ekībhāvo bhaved yatra yuganaddhaṃ taducyate || Pk_5.2 ||
children.translated_text: where unification arises — that is called <s>yuganaddha</s> (union). (Pk 5.2)

children.text: saṅkleśaṃ vyavadānaṃ ca jñātvā tu paramārthataḥ |
children.translated_text: Having known defilement (<s>saṅkleśa</s>) and purification (<s>vyavadāna</s>) in the ultimate sense,

children.text: ekībhāvaṃ tu yo vettiṃ sa vetti yuganaddhakam || Pk_5.3 ||
children.translated_text: one who knows their unification — that one knows <s>yuganaddha</s> (union). (Pk 5.3)
The conception of entities with form (<s>sākāra</s>) and the imagination of formlessness (<s>nirākāra</s>) —

children.text: ekīkṛtya cerad yogī sa vetti yuganaddhakam || Pk_5.4 ||
children.translated_text: having unified these, if the <s>yogī</s> practices, he knows <s>yuganaddha</s> (union). (Pk 5.4)

children.text: grāhyaṃ ca grāhakaṃ caiva dvidhā buddhirna vidyate |
children.translated_text: The grasped and the grasper — twofold cognition does not exist;

children.text: abhinnatā bhaved yatra tadāha yuganaddhakam || Pk_5.5 ||
children.translated_text: where non-duality arises — that is called <s>yuganaddha</s> (union). (Pk 5.5)
One who, having abandoned the views of eternalism (<s>śāśvata</s>) and annihilationism (<s>uccheda</s>), proceeds —

children.text: yuganaddhakramākhyaṃ vai tattvaṃ vetti sa paṇḍitaḥ || Pk_5.6 ||
children.translated_text: truly knows the <s>tattva</s> (reality) called <s>yuganaddha-krama</s> (the stage of union). || Pk_5.6 ||
Having known the unity of <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom) and <s>karuṇā</s> (compassion), where one engages,

children.text: yuganaddha iti khyātaḥ kramo 'yaṃ buddhagocaraḥ || Pk_5.7 ||
children.translated_text: this stage, known as <s>yuganaddha</s> (union), is the domain of the <s>Buddhas</s>. || Pk_5.7 ||
Having known everything in brief through the equipoise of <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom) and <s>upāya</s> (skillful means),

children.text: yatra sthito mahāyogī tad bhaved yuganaddhakam || Pk_5.8 ||
children.translated_text: that state in which the great <s>yogī</s> abides is <s>yuganaddha</s> (union). || Pk_5.8 ||
Where neither <s>sopadhiśeṣa</s> (with remainder)

children.text: ityevaṃ kalpanā nāsti tat taddhi yuganaddhakam || Pk_5.9 ||
children.translated_text: nor <s>anupadhiśeṣa</s> (without remainder) — such conceptual distinctions do not exist — that indeed is <s>yuganaddha</s> (union). || Pk_5.9 ||
Where <s>pudgala-nairātmya</s> (selflessness of the person) and <s>dharma-nairātmya</s> (selflessness of phenomena) —
freedom from such conceptual elaboration is the characteristic of <s>yuganaddha</s> (union). || Pk_5.10 ||
Having known through the stages, the knower of reality realizes <s>svādhiṣṭhāna</s> (self-consecration) and <s>prabhāsvara</s> (clear light);

children.text: tayoreva samājaṃ yad yuganaddhakramo hyayam || Pk_5.11 ||
children.translated_text: their very conjunction is this <s>yuganaddha-krama</s> (stage of union). || Pk_5.11 ||
Through <s>piṇḍagrāha</s> (aggregate grasping) and its analysis, entry into the abode of <s>tathatā</s> (suchness),

children.text: utthānaṃ ca tato yatra samantād yuganaddhakam || Pk_5.12 ||
children.translated_text: and arising therefrom — where all of this is complete, that is <s>yuganaddha</s> (union). || Pk_5.12 ||

children.text: saṃvṛtiṃ paramārthaṃ ca pṛthag jñātvā vibhāgataḥ |
children.translated_text: Having known <s>saṃvṛti</s> (conventional truth) and <s>paramārtha</s> (ultimate truth) separately and distinctly,

children.text: saṃmīlanaṃ bhaved yatra yuganaddhaṃ taducyate || Pk_5.13 ||
children.translated_text: where their merging occurs, that is called <s>yuganaddha</s> (union). || Pk_5.13 ||

children.text: tathātalambanaṃ naiva vyutthānaṃ yatra naiva hi |
children.translated_text: Where there is neither clinging to <s>tathatā</s> (suchness) nor arising from meditation,

children.text: yuganaddhaṃ bhavet tacca yogināṃ padamavyayam || Pk_5.14 ||
children.translated_text: that is <s>yuganaddha</s> (union), the imperishable state of the <s>yogīs</s>. || Pk_5.14 ||
Free from the two states of 'asleep' and 'awake',
the Teacher declares <s>yuganaddha</s> (union) to be devoid of sleep and waking. || Pk_5.15 ||
For whom there is absolutely no meditation or non-meditation in any way,
that <s>yogī</s>, established in <s>yuganaddha</s> (union), is free from existence and non-existence. || Pk_5.16 ||
Liberated from non-mindfulness and mindfulness, characterized by perpetual arising,
the <s>yogī</s> established in <s>yuganaddha-krama</s> (the stage of union) moves about at will. || Pk_5.17 ||
Free from passion and non-passion, embodying supreme bliss,
the one who realizes <s>yuganaddha</s> (union) remains thus until the end of <s>saṃsāra</s>. || Pk_5.18 ||
Having made effect and cause non-different in their essential nature,

children.text: yā sthitiryogināṃ buddhā yuganaddhaṃ vadanti tat || Pk_5.19 ||
children.translated_text: that abiding of the <s>yogīs</s> — the <s>Buddhas</s> declare it to be <s>yuganaddha</s> (union). || Pk_5.19 ||
This is the <s>utpatti-krama</s> (generation stage), and this is the <s>utpanna-krama</s> (completion stage) —
where there is oneness of these two, that is called <s>yuganaddha</s> (union). || Pk_5.20 ||
'This deity is pure, this one is impure' —

children.text: iti yā kalpanābhinnā yatra tad yuganaddhakam || Pk_5.21 ||
children.translated_text: where such conceptual distinction is dissolved, that is <s>yuganaddha</s> (union). || Pk_5.21 ||
'Having form' and 'formless' — through the abandonment of this dual conceptualization,

children.text: yaḥśāntiṃ vetti yogīndraḥ sa prāpto yuganaddhakam || Pk_5.22 ||
children.translated_text: the lord of <s>yogīs</s> who knows peace has attained <s>yuganaddha</s> (union). || Pk_5.22 ||

children.text: evaṃ vai yaḥ sthito yogī yuganaddhakrame sthitaḥ |
children.translated_text: Thus indeed, the <s>yogī</s> who abides, established in <s>yuganaddha-krama</s> (the stage of union),

children.text: ucyate sa hi sarvajñaḥ tattvadarśī ca viśvadhṛk || Pk_5.23 ||
children.translated_text: is called omniscient, a seer of reality, and upholder of the universe. || Pk_5.23 ||
Fully awakened through the net of illusion, one who has crossed the ocean of <s>saṃsāra</s>,
the great <s>yogī</s>, having accomplished all that is to be done, is established in the path of the two truths. || Pk_5.24 ||

children.text: buddhatvaṃ vajrasattvatvaṃ sarvaiśvaryaṃ tathaiva ca || Pk_5.25 |
children.translated_text: <s>Buddhahood</s>, the state of <s>Vajrasattva</s> (diamond being), and likewise all sovereignty. || Pk_5.25 |
The <s>vajropama-samādhi</s> (diamond-like concentration) is indeed the <s>niṣpanna-krama</s> (completion stage),
and the <s>vajropama-samādhi</s> (diamond-like concentration) is also said to be non-dual. || Pk_5.26 ||

body.translated_text: This itself is non-dual knowledge, <s>apratiṣṭhita-nirvṛti</s> (non-abiding nirvāṇa),

children.translated_text: Words such as <s>anutpāda</s> (non-arising) and others are indicators of non-dual knowledge;

children.text: asyaiva vācakāḥ sarve nānyat tatrābhidhīyate || Pk_5.27 ||
children.translated_text: all of them designate this very thing — nothing else is referred to therein. || Pk_5.27 ||
The <s>siddhi</s> (attainment) whose nature is <s>Mahāmudrā</s> (the Great Seal), free from the positions of existence and non-existence —

children.text: anenaiva gatā buddhā gaṅgāyāḥ sikatopamāḥ || Pk_5.28 ||
children.translated_text: by this very path, <s>Buddhas</s> as numerous as the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s> have gone. || Pk_5.28 ||
The great <s>yogī</s>, striving, established in the stage of <s>yuganaddha</s> (union),

children.text: bhāvayed yuganaddhaṃ tu caryāṃ cāpi tadanvayām || Pk_5.29 ||
children.translated_text: should cultivate <s>yuganaddha</s> (union) and also the <s>caryā</s> (conduct) that accords with it. || Pk_5.29 ||

children.text: yathātmani tathā śatrau yathā bhāryā tathātmajā |
children.translated_text: As toward oneself, so toward an enemy; as toward a wife, so toward a daughter;

children.text: yathā mātā tathā vaiśyā yathā ḍombī tathā dvijā || Pk_5.30 ||
