children.translated_text: as toward a mother, so toward a prostitute; as toward an outcaste woman, so toward a brahmin woman. || Pk_5.30 ||

children.text: yathā vastraṃ tathā carma yathā ratnaṃ tathā tuṣam |
children.translated_text: As toward cloth, so toward leather; as toward a jewel, so toward chaff;

children.text: yathā mūtraṃ tathā madyaṃ yathā bhaktaṃ tathā śakṛt || Pk_5.31 ||
children.translated_text: as toward urine, so toward liquor; as toward food, so toward excrement. || Pk_5.31 ||
As toward sweet-smelling camphor, so toward the odor born of filth;

children.text: yathā stutikaraṃ vākyaṃ tathā vākyaṃ jugupsitam || Pk_5.32 ||
children.translated_text: as toward words of praise, so toward words of disgust. || Pk_5.32 ||

children.text: yathā rudrastathā vajrī yathā rātrīstathā divā |
children.translated_text: As toward <s>Rudra</s>, so toward the <s>Vajra</s>-holder; as toward night, so toward day;

children.text: yathā svapnaṃ tathā dṛṣṭaṃ yathā naṣṭaṃ tathā sthitam || Pk_5.33 ||
children.translated_text: as toward a dream, so toward what is seen; as toward what is lost, so toward what remains. || Pk_5.33 ||

children.text: yathā saukhyaṃ tathā duḥkhaṃ yathā duṣṭastathā sutaḥ |
children.translated_text: As toward happiness, so toward suffering; as toward a wicked person, so toward a good son;

children.text: yathāvīcistathā svargastathā puṇyaṃ tu pāpakam || Pk_5.34 ||
children.translated_text: as toward <s>Avīci</s> (hell), so toward heaven; likewise toward merit and sin. || Pk_5.34 ||

children.text: evaṃ jñātvā cared jñānī nirviśaṅkastu sarvakṛt |
children.translated_text: Having known thus, the wise one should act without hesitation, accomplishing all;
having attained the <s>pracchannavrata</s> (secret vow), all accomplishments are perfected. || Pk_5.35 ||

body.text:
prakāśya puṇyaṃ yat prāptaṃ pañcakramamanuttaram |
anena krīḍatāṃ loko yuganaddhasamādhinā || iti || Pk_5.36 ||
body.translated_text: By the merit obtained through proclaiming the unsurpassed <s>Pañcakrama</s> (Five Stages), may the world delight in <s>yuganaddha-samādhi</s> (the concentration of union). || Thus || Pk_5.36 ||
The <s>Yuganaddha-krama</s> (Stage of Union), the fifth, is completed.
This is the work of the master <s>Nāgārjuna</s>. The extent of this treatise is thirty-five verses.
|| The <s>Pañcakrama</s> (Five Stages) is completed. ||

children.translated_text: Having known the unity of <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom) and <s>karuṇā</s> (compassion), where one engages,
this stage, known as <s>yuganaddha</s> (union), is the domain of the <s>Buddhas</s>.

body.translated_text: (<s>Pañcakrama</s>, 5.7)

children.translated_text: With the form of intensely deep, stable, dense sound, the whirling <s>Mandara</s> mountain —
resembling the feet of glaciers situated amidst the waves of the agitated, steadfast deep,
at glorious <s>Potalaka</s>, resounding with the echoes of profound exposition,
encircled by the splendor of dense, radiant rays — may <s>Lokeśvara</s> protect you!

body.translated_text: (In the <s>Subhāṣitaratnakoṣa</s>, by <s>Vidyākara</s>)

children.text: na satyā nāsatyā na ca tadubhayī nāpyanubhayī
children.translated_text: Neither true, nor untrue, nor both, nor neither,
beyond description, consisting of the most excellent of all forms — such is the <s>Madhyamaka</s> understanding.
The <s>Jina</s> (Victor) is the Teacher, and she is the reality of the world, both moving and still;
the goddess of self-awareness, beloved of <s>Sukhavajra</s> (bliss-diamond), is victorious!

body.translated_text: (In the <s>Amṛtakaṇikā</s>, the commentary on the <s>Nāmasaṃgīti</s>, by <s>Raviśrī</s>)

children.text: ye dharmā hetuprabhavā hetusteṣāṃ tathāgato hyavadat |
children.translated_text: Those <s>dharmas</s> which arise from causes — their cause the <s>Tathāgata</s> has declared,

children.text: teṣāṃ ca yo nirodha evaṃvādī mahāśramaṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and also their cessation — thus proclaims the great <s>śramaṇa</s> (ascetic).

body.translated_text: May there be well-being.
